title: Dynamical modelling and the origin of gas turbulence in z ∼ 4.5 galaxies
question: Derive the structural properties of the gas, stars and dark matter halos of four z ~ 4.5 [CII] discs via rotation-curve mass decomposition, and test whether stellar feedback or gravitational instabilities drive their turbulence

recipe.goal: make dust-continuum image and [CII] moment-0 map
recipe.method: separate line from continuum, make a dust-continuum image and a [CII] datacube, integrate cube along velocity for the [CII] total emission map
assumptions: [CII] emission traces the total gas distribution, so gas surface density is proportional to [CII] surface brightness

recipe.goal: fit 2D Sersic profiles to [CII] and dust maps
recipe.method: 2D Sersic fit with model convolved to data resolution, DYNESTY sampling
key_parameters: free: R_eff, I_e, centre (x0, y0), ellipticity, PA, for both gas and dust
Sersic index fixed to 1 for all fits except BRI1335-0417 dust (free); a preliminary free-n fit varied n within 0.2 and 10.0
SGP38326-1 and -2 fitted simultaneously; small companion SGP38326-3 masked
sigma = standard deviation of residual map after subtracting the moment 0 map rotated by 180 deg
assumptions: discs razor-thin, inclination from ellipticity (cos^2 i = 1 - eps)
gas disc scale length R_gas = R_eff,[CII]/1.678 for an exponential profile

recipe.goal: adopt rotation curves and dispersion profiles
recipe.method: use 3DBarolo kinematic profiles (rotation curves and velocity dispersion) from the previous paper

recipe.goal: correct rotation curves for pressure support
recipe.method: asymmetric drift correction assuming an exponential gas disc with the best-fit [CII] scale length, numerically differentiating ln sigma
assumptions: isotropic velocity ellipsoid and disc thickness constant with radius

recipe.goal: decompose circular speed into stars, gas and DM
recipe.method: fit V_c(R) = sqrt(V_star^2 + V_gas^2 + V_DM^2) with Sersic-stellar (Terzic and Graham density-potential), razor-thin exponential gas disc and NFW halo components
key_parameters: log M* uniform 9 - 12; stellar Sersic n uniform 0.2 - 10; R_eff,* uniform between R_eff of dust and of [CII]
M_gas = L_CO x gas_norm, with gas_norm uniform 0 - 10
NFW concentration fixed at 3.4; baryon fraction uniform in log between 1e-6 and 0.187 (log f_bar -6 to -0.73)
BRI1335-0417: baryon fraction fixed to the cosmological value in the fiducial model
assumptions: gas follows an exponential razor-thin disc with the [CII] scale length
stellar component spherical with Sersic light profile

recipe.goal: derive gas fraction, baryonic radius and disc fraction
recipe.method: compute f_gas = M_gas/M_bar, effective baryonic radius (half baryonic mass) and disc fraction (baryons to DM inside that radius) from the decomposition; place galaxies on SFR vs M* plane
assumptions: SFRs from IR luminosity converted to a Chabrier IMF; stellar masses from the decomposition

recipe.goal: compare dispersions with gravity- and feedback-driven turbulence models
recipe.method: compare observed velocity dispersion vs SFR to the two Krumholz et al. scenarios (gravitational instability only; stellar feedback only) at circular speeds spanning the sample
assumptions: Toomre Q marginally stable in both scenarios

recipe.goal: compare SNII energy input with observed turbulent energy
recipe.method: E_SN = eta * E_SNII * xi * h / sigma compared with E_turb = 3/2 M_gas sigma^2; eta = 1 gives the maximum injectable energy, identity lines show eta
key_parameters: E_SNII = 10^51 erg per SNII; xi = 0.01 per Msun x SFR for a Chabrier IMF
thin disc h = 0.3 kpc and thick disc h = 1.0 kpc
assumptions: SNIa neglected as high-z galaxies are SNII dominated
line-of-sight dispersion isotropic; thermal broadening negligible

recipe.method: compare with the local baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (external circular speed = mean of the outer two resolution-independent elements), the ETG analogue Tully-Fisher relation (stellar and baryonic mass), and the SHMR
assumptions: for the ETG relation the gas is assumed fully converted into stars by z = 0 when adding gas to stellar mass
